chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Aban, not knowing except that it was mentioned from Abu Hamza, who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), whenever he saw a funeral approaching, would say: 'The praise is to Allah, Who did not make me from the perished masses.'

key_terms.السَّوَاد: The masses / the crowd (specifically referring to the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn say when seeing a funeral?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) utilized this supplication to cultivate *huzn* (spiritual melancholy) and gratitude for the respite of life, distinguishing the living from the 'perished masses' (*al-sawad al-mukhtaram*) who have passed into the grave. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on internalizing the reality of death to motivate spiritual preparation, a concept deeply rooted in the Imam's role as the teacher of du'as and supplications.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mgheira, from Aban, not knowing except that it was mentioned from Abu Hamza who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws </sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, whenever he<sup>asws</sup> saw the funeral (coffin) to have faced, said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Who did not Make me<sup>asws</sup> to be from the perished masses’.
en.sarwar: 1. I do not know about him more of his name - from abu Hamzah who has said the following:
“Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, on seeing a dead body brought near, would say, ‘All praise belongs to Allah who has not brought my life to an end.’”
